title: Playback investigation and sampled-trace runbook - Aug 11 2025
content:
Purpose and context:

Short: capture an easily repeatable playback that surfaces the 99th/99.9th latency regression we saw on 2025-08-06 after the kernel selection change. Goal is to create a small runbook for reproducing with sampled traces and identify deterministic signals (kv-cache misses, batch size spikes, blocking IO).

Background notes (quick):
- Regression first observed in canary for model-gpt-1-8b-quant on dedicated-pool-west. 99.9th latency up ~2.1x for sequences >1024 tokens.
- Hypothesis A: new kernel chooser falls back to slower NVMemory path for long sequences when batch composition mixes short+long requests.
- Hypothesis B: prefix KV cache invalidation (race) under mixed batching causes full KV recompute, causing token stall for affected requests.
- Hypothesis C: storage reads (checkpoint sharding) cause occasional blocking when batch slots align with evicted segments.

What we did today (Aug 11):
- Collected 1200 sampled traces from the affected canary over a 3h window (02:00-05:00 UTC). Sampling configured at 0.3% global + 5% for high-latency flows (>= 500ms).
- Built a reduced request corpus of 48 requests representing seq lengths: [64, 256, 1024, 1536]. Mix ratio based on observed traffic: 50% short, 30% mid, 20% long.
- Implemented a deterministic playback harness (playback harness v0.3) that replays requests in original arrival order with preserved nonce headers to route to the same model shard.
- Ran parallel replays at target throughput 75% of observed peak to force real scheduler behavior.

Commands / quick repro (for devs):
- Export traces and corpus: ./tools/trace-export --from=2025-08-06T01:00Z --to=2025-08-06T04:00Z --sampled-only --min-latency-ms=200 --out=./tmp/corpus-aug06.json
- Start local playback harness (k8s exec into bench-runner): ./run_playback.sh --corpus ./tmp/corpus-aug06.json --target-qps 420 --preserve-order --route model-gpt-1-8b-quant
- Capture runtime metrics: ./scripts/collect-runtime-metrics.sh --labels "playback-aug11" --prom-endpoint http://prom:9090

Observed signals (first-pass):
- During playback reproducer, 99.9th latency increased from ~1.6s to ~3.5s for long requests (1536).
- KV cache hit-rate for affected shard fell from 98.6% to 82.4% when a short-request burst preceded a long request (correlated with batch boundary realignment).
- GPU kernel selection log (debug) shows frequent switch from optimized-attn-v2 -> fallback-attn-v1 when batch contains mixed seq lengths; fallback kernels have 2.8x slower per-token perf on our hardware.
- I/O stats show 40-60ms spikes on /checkpoint/shard-7 when playback iterates through a rare weight slice; manifests only when batch alignment causes concurrent access across two replicas.

Key traces (snippets):
- Trace A (high-level): requestId=rid_7f9k, arrival=2025-08-06T02:34:12Z, seqLen=1536, batchIndex=3, kernel=fall-back-attn-v1, kv_hit=false, latency=3523ms
- Trace B (control): requestId=rid_2a4b, arrival=2025-08-06T02:34:11Z, seqLen=64, batchIndex=0, kernel=optimized-attn-v2, kv_hit=true, latency=84ms
- Observed pattern: short->short->long (when long lands at batch tail) triggers kernel chooser path that evaluates batch max len incorrectly due to stale per-slot metadata (race window ~3-7ms).

Interim conclusions:
- Most likely root cause = combination of kernel chooser bug + KV cache invalidation race under mixed-batch compositions. Either alone would not explain magnitude.
- Reproducible in playback when we force the same arrival-order and inter-arrival spacing; less obvious when we randomize order.

Immediate mitigations to try (small, quick):
- Patch kernel chooser to use atomic read of per-slot max_seq metadata (hotfix candidate) — PR referenced below.
- Increase sampling of slow traces in canary to 2% until patch is deployed.
- Temporary routing: prefer homogeneous batching by size for canary traffic (route long-reqs to dedicated long-only queue).

Planned next steps and owners (timeline):
- (Today) Marco: produce stripped-down unit test that simulates mixed-batch boundaries (due EOD 2025-08-12).
- (Tomorrow) Aisha: land playback harness improvements to preserve per-slot metadata ordering and add deterministic sleeper to reproduce the 3-7ms race window (PR #6789 review). Target 2025-08-13.
- (48h) Lena/Devon: prototype KV-cache guard to serialize cache-update for slots with >1024 seq (performance impact expected; will run A/B). Start 2025-08-13, initial results 2025-08-15.
- (72h) Ops: enable 2% slow-trace sampling for canary and keep monitoring for 7 days. Contact SRE for additional retention if needed.

Open questions (to discuss in Thursday perf sync):
- If kernel choice is the main offender, can we add a fast-path to prefer optimized-attn even when mixed if estimated cost delta small? Tradeoffs?
- How much perf hit does KV-cache guard introduce for homogeneous workloads? Need microbench estimates.
- Are there lower-level memory fences we can add that avoid global lock but still make per-slot metadata consistent across batch assembly threads? (SSO: look at atomic_t vs relaxed read in slot_metadata.h)

Data attached in artifacts:
- playback results: artifacts/playback-aug11-results.csv (columns: req_id, seq_len, batch_pos, kernel, kv_hit, latency_ms, gpu_util)
- sample traces: artifacts/sampled-traces-aug11.ndjson (1K lines, trimmed)

Quick TODO checklist (for whoever picks this up):
- [ ] Re-run playback with single-queue homogeneous routing and compare 99.9th
- [ ] Add atomic read fix to kernel chooser in staging and run microbench
- [ ] Add KV-cache metric tags to Prom: kvcache.slots.updated, kvcache.invalidations.count
- [ ] Prepare short postmortem draft if hotfix not applied within 72h

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep playback corpus size small — large corpuses make iteration slow. Aim for ~50-100 requests per run with representative mix.
- When reproducing in CI, add deterministic seed so the harness orders match traces.
- Slack thread: #perf-serving-runtime (see thread starting 2025-08-06) — we should post a short summary there after this doc.

Appendix: quick sketch of the deterministic playback harness (high level)
- Input: sampled-ndjson of traces with original arrival timestamps, request payload, and routing headers
- Stage 1: normalize payloads (strip non-deterministic headers), compute inter-arrival times relative to first request
- Stage 2: open X worker connections to model shard, preserve nonce header to keep routing stable
- Stage 3: replay requests with preserved inter-arrival, optionally accelerate clock (scale factor) but maintain microsecond ordering
- Stage 4: capture server-side debug logs and append trace id -> local playback id mapping (for follow-up)

If you take this on, ping me on Slack or add notes inline. I will iterate the runbook after we validate hotfix impact.

End of notes.
